# The cubic capacity inequality is not true for arbitrary probability laws
uniform-convex-body distribution from the new coordinate-capacity route.
It is not a counterexample for any uniform convex body or for OC.

For a law Z on the probability simplex {z>=0:sum z_i=1}, define

    c_i=inf_{t>0, P(Z_i<=t)>0} t/sqrt(P(Z_i<=t)).

The tempting assertion sum c_i^2+2 product c_i<=1 is false.

## 1. An existing exact coupling certificate

The archived file `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/beta_coupling_exact_certificate_root.json` specifies
399 positive rational masses on triples (i,j,k), with 0<=i,j,k<200.
Their total is one. With n=200, its exact identities are

    sum_{triples with first index i} mass=(2i+1)/n^2,
    sum_{triples with second or third index j} mass=2(2j+1)/n^2,
    [2(i+1)+(j+1)+(k+1)]/n<=273/100.

the contributor rechecked all these identities using rational arithmetic on
2026-09-30. They are also checked by the archived exact certifier
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/certify_beta_coupling_exact_root.py`.

Symmetrize the last two indices by an independent fair interchange.
Each of the three coordinate-bin marginals is then (2i+1)/n^2. In bin
[i/n,(i+1)/n], draw the coordinate with density proportional to 2x;
the three conditional draws may be independent. Every resulting coordinate
U_i has the exact Beta(2,1) CDF P(U_i<=t)=t^2 for 0<=t<=1. The upper
bin endpoints give, for every outcome,

    2U_1+U_2+U_3<=273/100.

This is a continuum coupling constructed from a finite rational certificate,
not a numerical approximation to its marginals or its support bound.

## 2. A law on the simplex violating the cubic

Set

    p=(200,100,100)/273,       V_i=p_i U_i.

The coupling gives sum V_i<=1. Define

    Z_1=V_1+(1-sum V_i),       Z_2=V_2,       Z_3=V_3.

Then Z belongs to the probability simplex and Z_i>=V_i. Consequently,
for every t>0,

    P(Z_i<=t)<=P(V_i<=t)<=t^2/p_i^2.

Its capacities satisfy c_i>=p_i. The cubic is increasing in nonnegative
coordinates, whereas exact arithmetic gives

    sum p_i^2+2 product p_i-1
      =33583/20346417>0.

Thus this actual law violates the proposed probability-only theorem.
Equivalently, the rational support test at q=(200/273,1,1) gives

    sum q_i^2-2 sum_i p_i product_{j!=i}q_j
      =-142/74529<0.

This obstruction applies to a proof that keeps only coordinate CDF bounds
and sum Z_i=1, even if each marginal is obtained by dominating a scaled
Beta(2,1) variable. The uniform distribution on an actual triangle or other
convex body contains additional information. Neither the proved stochastic
triangle theorem nor the remaining ordinary quadrilateral conjecture is
contradicted.
